channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Managers’ pay rise blocked at 28 trusts, but ICBs spared
item.description: Very senior managers at 28 struggling trusts will not receive this year’s 3 per cent pay rise, ministers have confirmed.

item.title: ‘Shocking’ rise in maternal readmissions revealed
item.description: The rate of women readmitted to hospital within six weeks of giving birth has risen by more than a third in less than three years, HSJ analysis of unpublished data suggests.

item.title: Victims demand tougher restrictions on snooping
item.description: Victims of the Southport and Nottingham attacks have told ministers and NHS leaders that far stricter, more robust processes are needed to stop staff snooping on patient records – and that actions outlined so far are not enough.

item.title: NHSE warns ICBs over staffing and capability gaps
item.description: NHS England criticised staffing and capacity issues at several integrated care boards, a year after instructing them to cut their staffing by half.

item.title: Vulnerable patients’ long dental waits ‘buried’
item.description: NHS England has been accused of continuing to “bury” evidence of the very long waits for dental treatment endured by people with complex needs, the British Dental Association has said.

item.title: Palantir must clear FDP benefits claims
item.description: NHS England has asked to review any claims made by Palantir about the effectiveness of the federated data platform before they are published, following concerns from the statistics watchdog.

item.title: Mackey: ‘Let’s stop directors sitting on multiple boards’
item.description: Directors sitting on multiple hospital trust boards without a clear purpose have “shrunk the pool” and are creating “too much of a closed mentality”, Sir Jim Mackey has told MPs.

item.title: Exclusive: New agency to host thousands of NHSE staff
item.description: The government is today confirming it will create a new national agency to employ thousands of staff in NHS regional teams, while pressing on with abolishing NHS England by April next year.

item.title: DHSC and NHSE consultancy bill surges 60%
item.description: Consultancy spending by the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS England leapt by almost 60 per cent last year – despite a government pledge to halve such expenditure.

item.title: Former ‘outstanding’ trust’s A&E rated ‘inadequate’ for safety
item.description: Urgent and emergency care services have been rated “inadequate” for safety at a trust that was rated “outstanding” until July.

item.title: 21 patients died after heatwave ambulance delays
item.description: Twenty-one patients died after delayed responses from an ambulance service during June’s heatwave amid a huge spike in serious calls, board papers show.

item.title: Hospital rebuilds face further delay
item.description: Two new hospitals are likely to be further delayed and cost an additional £200m if plans for major service reconfiguration are pursued, trust bosses have warned.

item.title: Ambulances without paramedics still attending thousands of calls
item.description: Three in 20 ambulances reaching patients with a life-threatening emergency have no paramedic as part of their crew in large parts of the country, an HSJ analysis of the latest data has discovered.

item.title: Trial targets missed despite ‘hit’ claim
item.description: The government is missing two of its five clinical trials targets, despite declaring last month it had “hit” its headline goal on trial set-up.

item.title: Deeper financial cuts would impact patient safety, warns trust
item.description: A trust has all but conceded it cannot meet its financial plan this year, as finding the required savings would most likely be “at the expense of patient safety”.

item.title: Closing two of county’s three maternity units best for safety, says review
item.description: Closing two of three consultant-led maternity units run by a hospital group is the best option for safety and staffing, a review by senior local clinical leaders has concluded.

item.title: Revealed: The huge happiness gap between frontline and support staff
item.description: Those working in the frontline care divisions of hospital trusts are much likelier to be unhappy at work than their peers employed within the support divisions of the same provider, HSJ analysis has found.

item.title: Ex-minister with breast cancer to advise on national plan
item.description: A former health minister living with incurable breast cancer has been appointed as the government’s “Cancer Adviser”.

item.title: Trust exit packages double to nearly 10,000
item.description: The number of staff leaving trusts with exit packages more than doubled last year, to almost 9,300, accounts show.

item.title: NHS bosses to rethink constitutional targets
item.description: The body representing most NHS organisations plans to start work on rethinking the service’s national waiting time standards for “the NHS of the future”.
